files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Added

- manager/HR can end a running approved employee absence early (end-early
  with mandatory reason + CAS, audit `absence_manager_shortened`, owner +
  HR-office notification); elapsed days stay recorded — complements manager
  cancel which removes the whole period
- absence form shows the actual vacation-day consumption for multi-day
  requests ("This request uses N vacation days."), computed server-side
  per the employee's working-time model
- dashboard hours-at-a-glance tiles include the approved-absence credit in
  the actual hours, with a "incl. X h absence credit" footnote, matching
  the overtime balance math
- prior-year carryover row renamed to "Prior-year carryover left"
  (de: "Resturlaub Vorjahr") and shows "(expired)" once the transfer
  deadline has passed
- people overview "Approved upcoming" column documents that it sums
  approved vacation days per the employee's working-time model
- companion app: employee-absences manager surface (employee picker → list
  → flag-gated shorten/cancel with CAS + mandatory reason), server-side
  day-consumption preview in create and manager record forms, absence
  credit in hours glance, "Prior-year carryover left" label + "(expired)"
  marker, record form defaults to server "today"
- absence payload carries additive `canShorten` flag for owners
  (server-computed eligibility; older servers fall back to the
  isCurrent+approved derivation)
- **opt-in half-day for non-vacation absence types**: new admin multiselect
  "Allow half days for" (`half_day_enabled_types`, default `["vacation"]` —
  byte-identical legacy behaviour). Enabled types get the day-length control
  on the manager record form, the employee request form, and the mobile
  companion (manager record + employee create screens); the server debits
  `days = schedule weight × 0.5`, rejects fractions on non-enabled types
  loudly (`HALF_DAY_TYPE_NOT_ENABLED`) and on multi-day ranges
  (`HALF_DAY_RANGE_FORBIDDEN`), keeps stored fractions on reason-only edits
  and vacation→sick conversion, and preserves them across the
  schedule-recompute repair. Custom absence types can be opted in
  individually; `overtime_comp`, `parental_leave` and entitlement-bound
  types stay excluded (their {0.25,0.5,0.75} contract is untouched)
- working-time-model editor section "Break rules (stricter)": per-model
  break tiers (`afterHours` → `breakMinutes`, ≤8) and minimum countable
  break length — the central policy engine already merged them as
  `max(law, org, model)`; malformed stored fragments prefill tolerantly
  with a cleanup hint so a save self-heals
- strict write validation for all `break_rules` keys on working-time
  models (tiers, floor, break_policy, auto_fallback_minutes,
  allow_sunday_work) + completed key registry so near-miss names reject
  with 400 instead of persisting silently; save responses echo the
  normalized stored document
- **opt-in `cap_overhang` deduction mode** (org policy `deduction_mode`,
  model override, `model ?? org ?? strict` resolution): automatic breaks
  record only the overhang minutes beyond the crossed threshold so the
  recorded net lands exactly on it (9h31m → 31 min, net 9h00m); admin
  radio with informed-consent copy + CONFIRM_REQUIRED gate on the
  strict→cap transition, capped portions tail-placed `[end−d, end]`,
  flagged `capped:true`/`deduction_mode` in the breaks JSON, sub-floor
  exempt from the manual countability floor, and audit-logged
  (`deduction_mode`, `capped`, `overhang_seconds`)
- stale same-entry automatic break portions are now trimmed newest-first
  when a manual break is recorded afterwards (manual reality is never
  rewritten)
- `deductionMode` additive key in `capabilities.compliance` and the web
  `complianceParams` bootstrap (strict fallback for older servers);
  mobile companion computes the statutory requirement on the declared
  net (span − recorded breaks) inside `validateManualEntry`, fixing the
  gross-span 45-min demand on 9h0Xm entries

### Fixed

- database lock rows left behind by killed requests no longer block
  catalog and admin mutations for up to an hour: acquisitions now sweep
  provably-expired rows once and retry (genuine contention unchanged)
- **automatic break deduction evaluated on the resulting net working
  time** (minimal-consistent fixpoint `required(P − d) ≤ d`): a ~9h05m
  presence now inserts the statutory 30 min instead of 45 — the
  over-deduction reported by Cecilienstift Halberstadt; mobile companion
  computes the statutory requirement on the declared net (span −
  recorded breaks) instead of the gross span (9h0Xm + 30m break no
  longer demands 45)
- planned-hours credit no longer double-halves a **full** absence day that
  lands on a half-weight company holiday: the fraction is derived as
  `days ÷ single-day weight` instead of a literal `days ≈ 0.5` match (a full
  sick day at weight 0.5 was credited net×0.25 instead of net×0.5)
- stored `"false"`/`"0"` strings no longer stay truthy-active:
  `allow_sunday_work` (Sunday-work Freibrief), `weekday_schedule` `work`
  and break `paid` flags (an unpaid break could have been paid), and
  premium-category `enabled` now parse strict-bool — fail closed
- `auto_fallback_minutes` stored garbage falls back to the configured
  default instead of silently clamping to 15 minutes
- `overtimeRules` is now a bounded map-only document (≤8 KB);
  `break_rules` documents are capped at 32 KB
- clearing every editor-owned break rule on a model now actually clears
  them (paid-break flag and others previously survived an all-empty save)
- absence `days` now counts the employee's `weekday_schedule` work days
  instead of hardcoded Mon–Fri — part-time employees (e.g. 4-day model)
  were debited one day too many for every Mon–Fri vacation week; a repair
  step recomputes open absences (non-finalized months only, audit-logged,
  half-day safe); models without a weekday schedule keep Mon–Fri counting
- manager absence recording form defaults From/To to today instead of
  inheriting the one-month list-filter range
- shorten eligibility (owner + manager paths) now compares calendar dates
  instead of instants — on hosts whose PHP default timezone differs from
  the organisation timezone the started/ended guards could skew by up to
  a day, letting the action flags and the write guard disagree
- mobile: manager absence record no longer applies the server "today"
  only partially — a ref-guard was read after it was already overwritten,
  so the end-date default could stay on the device date
